raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary (human-written)
With pipeline parallelism enabled on XPU, TorchTitan enables pipeline_per_edge_p2p, but XCCL cannot split process groups for directed pipeline edges. This change disables per-edge P2P when the backend is XCCL. We tested the change on an XPU device and confirmed that it works.
## Why

`init_distributed` currently enables `pipeline_per_edge_p2p` whenever the pipeline parallel degree exceeds one. On XPU, the default backend is XCCL, which cannot split process groups for directed pipeline edges.

| Device | Backend | PP degree | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| XPU | XCCL | 2 | Per-edge P2P enabled | Disabled |
| CUDA | NCCL | 2 | Per-edge P2P enabled | Enabled |

## What changed

- Check the device's default distributed backend before configuring per-edge P2P.
- Disable the option for XCCL while preserving its behavior for other backends.

## Numerics / performance

No numerical or performance measurements have been collected yet. An XPU pipeline run is needed to validate training behavior.

## Testing

- Python syntax check and `git diff --check` passed before commit.
- Verified on an XPU device internally and it passed the XCCL test.

@tianyu-l  updated with fix for the lint error and added links to the upstream XCCL issues.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The XCCL gate is the right minimal shape. But the PR doesn't yet show the failure on `main`, and the workaround doesn't link the upstream gap. A maintainer still needs to review, since this touches core distributed init.

**What this PR does.** Since #4540, `init_distributed` turns on PyTorch's `dist_config.pipeline_per_edge_p2p` whenever PP > 1. That flag splits a communicator for each directed PP edge. This PR leaves the flag off when the device's default backend is `xccl`, so XPU runs use the shared PP process group for P2P, as they did before #4540.

**Example.**
```
device_type="xpu", PP=2, PyTorch exposes pipeline_per_edge_p2p
  main: pipeline_per_edge_p2p=True  -> per-edge group split on XCCL fails (per PR; error not shown)
  PR:   pipeline_per_edge_p2p=False -> P2P uses the shared PP group
device_type="xpu", PP=2, older PyTorch without the option
  main: RuntimeError("Pipeline parallelism requires a PyTorch version ...")
  PR:   no error (per-edge isn't needed on XCCL)
device_type="cuda" (NCCL): unchanged
```

### Must fix
1. **PR description.** It doesn't show the concrete failure on `main`. Please add the error and stack trace for XPU with PP=2, plus the PyTorch and oneCCL/XCCL versions, so a maintainer can check the root cause. Two sections also contradict each other: "Numerics / performance" says "An XPU pipeline run is needed to validate training behavior", while "Testing" says it was verified on XPU. Please say what was actually run (schedule, PP degree, number of steps) and whether the loss looked sane.
2. `torchtitan/distributed/utils.py:503-505` -- the workaround needs a TODO that links an upstream issue (see the inline comment).

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_distributed_utils.py:78` -- there is no XPU CI, so nothing would catch this gate being removed. One extra case in the existing `test_init_distributed_configures_pipeline_per_edge_p2p` parametrization would cover it: patch `default_device_backend_map` (or `device_type`) to resolve to `xccl` with PP=2 and expect `False`. Extend the existing test; don't add a new one.

### Questions
- Do recent PyTorch builds already report `supports_splitting` for `ProcessGroupXCCL`? If they do, the failure may depend on the version, and the gate should say which versions need it.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Placement and scope look right. `init_distributed` already owns this flag, and the change adds 5 lines with no new knobs.
- The backend lookup at line 504 is the same `default_device_backend_map` lookup that `_get_distributed_backend` does later, so both places agree on which backend is used. For `comm_config.backend="fake"` on an XPU host, the gate also turns per-edge P2P off. That only affects fake-PG dry runs, not real XCCL runs, which is acceptable.
- In eager mode, falling back to the shared PP group is what PP did before #4540. torchtitan's CUDA-graph paths are CUDA-only, so the deterministic per-edge FIFO ordering that CUDA-graph replay depends on doesn't apply to XPU.

</details>

Not verified: the XCCL split failure and whether newer PyTorch builds still have it (I couldn't inspect the installed PyTorch or run on XPU).

This works around a gap in PyTorch, not in torchtitan: either `ProcessGroupXCCL` lacks the comm splitting that per-edge P2P relies on, or PyTorch's per-edge path doesn't fall back for backends that can't split. Without a TODO, nobody will know when this vendor-specific `"xccl"` branch can come out of core code (CLAUDE.md principles 3 and 9).

Fix: make the comment a TODO that links an upstream issue (pytorch/pytorch, or intel/torch-xpu-ops if XCCL is the owner), e.g.

```python
# TODO(<upstream issue link>): XCCL cannot split process groups for directed
# PP edges. Remove this gate once per-edge P2P supports XCCL.
```

The proper fix belongs upstream. Per-edge P2P could check the backend's `supports_splitting` and fall back to the shared PP group. Then torchtitan wouldn't need a backend-name check.

detail.title: Avoid per-edge pipeline P2P with XCCL

files.patch:
@@ -500,11 +500,15 @@ def init_distributed(
     # Directed physical PP edges need independent, preinitialized communicator
     # FIFOs so eager execution and CUDA graph replay use deterministic ordering.
     # Older PyTorch versions do not expose this option.
+    # XCCL cannot split process groups for directed PP edges.
+    # TODO: upstream issue https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/186548 and
+    # https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/issues/5742
+    # Remove this gate once per-edge P2P supports XCCL.
+    backend = torch.distributed.Backend.default_device_backend_map.get(device_type)
+    use_per_edge_p2p = pipeline_parallel_degree > 1 and backend != "xccl"
     if hasattr(dist_config, "pipeline_per_edge_p2p"):
-        setattr(  # noqa: B010
-            dist_config, "pipeline_per_edge_p2p", pipeline_parallel_degree > 1
-        )
-    elif pipeline_parallel_degree > 1:
+        setattr(dist_config, "pipeline_per_edge_p2p", use_per_edge_p2p)  # noqa: B010
+    elif use_per_edge_p2p:
         raise RuntimeError(
             "Pipeline parallelism requires a PyTorch version that provides "
             "torch.distributed.distributed_c10d._config.pipeline_per_edge_p2p."

